Not the best game ever made, but its decent fun. Some tedious level designs, overdone grind compared to the first. Randomized maps feel better overall though and some areas are quit stunning. Some of the story areas and bosses are too gimmicky and not fun but others are pretty exciting. The first feels more like a cohesive game whereas this sequel feels like a bunch of random ideas thrown together and not really a natural evolution of the first. However once you're past your first campaign it gets quite good and theres a lot of variety in content.

One (Dark Horizon DLC) level absolutely kills the pacing, by adding a Zelda BotW style glider that makes navigation a total chore. Its only used in that area and is totally pointless.

Update: So the biggest gripe I have about the game (glider) seems to be a DLC addition to Nerud. I've changed this to a recommend and will add a DLC review, even if its not as strong as the first game.

Update 2: While I primarily use a gaming desktop, I was able to get a mostly solid 40 fps, and a very solid 30 fps on Steam Deck by setting "potato" graphics, intel XeSS scaling to ultra performance. Honestly the game still looks and plays way better than I expected on low end hardware. On high end though.. its pretty bad, as you'd expect from a UE5 game
